claim: tools/runner now resolves its repo root worktree-aware: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` first (accepts both a normal `.git` directory and a worktree's `.git` FILE with a `gitdir:` pointer), with the old isdir walk-up kept only as the fallback for a non-git directory — so heartbeats, directive reads, and run records land in a worktree's own untracked/ exactly as they do in the main checkout (T376 fixed the identical defect in tools/bakeoff.sh; the runner was not fixed with it).

design.defect: tools/runner:186 `_find_repo_root()` walked up from cwd looking for a `.git` DIRECTORY (os.path.isdir). In a git worktree `.git` is a FILE carrying a `gitdir:` pointer, so the walk ran to the filesystem root and returned None — silently disabling the heartbeat (untracked/heartbeat.jsonl gets nothing, so `managent liveness` cannot see the run), directive reads (`managent tell <id>` cannot reach a worker in a worktree), the run record (untracked/runs/<task>.json, T364), and the auto-claim path (which fell back to a relative bin/managent). The T447 race (2026-08-18) ran five lanes under tools/runner from a worktree at /tmp/weizigo/race-t447 and produced no heartbeats — the live failure. tools/bakeoff.sh had exactly this defect; T376 fixed it with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, which accepts both forms. The runner was not fixed with it.
design.fix: _find_repo_root() now runs `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` first (subprocess, 2 s timeout) and returns its stdout root on success; on any failure (not a git repository, no git on PATH, timeout) it falls back to the original walk-up for a `.git` directory. NOT os.path.isfile: a `.git` file's `gitdir:` may point outside the tree (the bundle's explicit bar), and the git command already answers correctly for both forms. The non-git fallback keeps the runner working as a bare command wrapper outside any repository — heartbeat/directive/run-record features are inert there, exactly as before the fix. Guard semantics (RSS/host-floor/wall/CPU/progress), identity handling, and the WORKER-CHANNEL behavior are untouched.
design.controls: tools/regression-runner-worktree.sh — three arms: (1) seeded: a runner launched from inside a fresh worktree resolves the WORKTREE as repo_root — a heartbeat line lands in the worktree's own untracked/heartbeat.jsonl with the right identifier; (2) seeded: a `pause` directive appended to the worktree's own directives.jsonl is READ (pending directives printed, exit 124); (3) null: the same run from the main checkout is unchanged — exactly one new heartbeat line with the T449-REG-NULL identifier (before/after count compare). Isolation: the worktree lives under /tmp/weizigo; seeded arms write only inside the scratch worktree; the null arm's single append to the main checkout's heartbeat.jsonl is the runner's normal per-invocation behavior and asserting it is the point. T448 start-up check: refuses to run while a stale fixture worktree is registered (a SIGKILLed previous run leaves the EXIT trap unrun).
design.test_first: RED first, then GREEN (standing tooling rule, AGENTS.md 2026-08-07): tools/regression-runner-worktree.sh was run against the UNFIXED runner and failed exactly on the defect — 'FAIL: seeded — no heartbeat with identifier T449-REG-CTRL in .../t449-reg-worktree/untracked/heartbeat.jsonl' and 'FAIL: seeded — directive not read (exit 0; pending-directives print: none)', with the null arm passing. After the _find_repo_root() fix the same script passed all three arms. The script was inherited from the T449.1 console (see notes) and re-run RED before the fix was applied.
